text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime.p99 latency spike on hosted-prod-us-east across /v1/stream and /v1/generate — threshold breached (p99 > 1.2s) · auto-page oncall

maria (oncall-sre): saw it, joining. initial checks: grafana link https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/latency?panel=streaming — p95 up ~300ms, p99 jumped to ~2.1s at 17:11:03

raj (eng-runtime): thanks. is this isolated to one model or pool? any recent rollouts?

maria (oncall-sre): routing shows increased queue depth on pool-us-east-2 (gpu-pool-7). error rate flat, CPU slightly higher on router service. no recent deploys in last 30m.

jim (eng-platform): autoscaler shows scale events failed to add nodes, `providerAPI: rate limit` seen in platform logs earlier — checking cloud provider console now.

ops-bot: NOTE: kube events: 5x `OOMKilled` on model-worker-7 pod over last 10m, restartCount=3

lucy (customer-support): getting first customer tickets for slow streaming responses (enterprise-acme). They've reported session stalls (UI spinner) for several minutes.

dan (product): flagging enterprise SLA risk. Dan -> can we notify acct reps if mitigation will take >10m?

maria (oncall-sre): quick triage steps: 1) confirm impact surface; 2) attempt routing fallback to warm-pool; 3) check KV cache saturation; 4) short-term scale-up if possible.

raj (eng-runtime): running quick health checks on the runtime:
```
curl -sS https://runtime.prod.internal/health | jq .
# checking kvcache metrics
curl -sS https://metrics.internal/api/series?m=kvcache.size
```

raj (eng-runtime): kvcache hit-rate dropped 40% around spike start — possible cache eviction thrash after pod restarts. also seeing long tail in `kv_cache_lookup` histogram (p99 ~120ms -> 700ms).

maria (oncall-sre): ok, probable combo: worker restarts -> cache misses -> increased compute per request -> queueing -> p99 spike. next: route traffic away from affected pool. jim can you force-route traffic to pool-us-east-1 warm nodes?

jim (eng-platform): on it. applying route override for 10m: `routingctl set-destination --route /v1/stream --from pool-us-east-2 --to pool-us-east-1 --weight 100`

ops-bot: ACTION: route override applied by jim at 17:12:05 — traffic now shifting.

maria (oncall-sre): starting targeted mitigation: mark bad pods unschedulable, cordon + drain, and restart pool service to re-warm caches.

raj (eng-runtime): small script to evict stale KV and warm top prefixes across pool-us-east-1:
```
# warm cache for top prefixes
for prefix in $(cat /opt/top_prefixes.txt); do
  seq 1 5 | xargs -I{} curl -sS -X POST https://hosted-api/v1/stream -d "{\"input\": \"$prefix test\"}" >/dev/null
done
```

lucy (customer-support): messaging: telling affected customers we are investigating and routing to alternative nodes; support ticket updated. will escalate to account team if latency persists. :white_check_mark:

maria (oncall-sre): monitoring p95/p99 now. grafana panel shows p99 across endpoints trending down after route override (~17:13:30) but streaming stalls (session timeouts) still reported.

tom (solutions): are streaming session reinstates failing on reconnect? any websocket errors?

raj (eng-runtime): log snippets from model-worker-7: `WARN: kvcache eviction miss for key shard-42`, `ERROR: grpc deadline exceeded`, and `Trace: forward_request latency=1.9s`. also a couple of `retryable error: too_many_inflight`

maria (oncall-sre): checking ingress queue metrics — per-host socket backlog high on a couple of router instances. scaling router horizontally as precaution.

jim (eng-platform): autoscaler hit provider limits earlier. requested temporary quota bump; meanwhile spinning up ephemeral router-standby pods on existing nodes. `kubectl scale deployment router --replicas=12`

ops-bot: scale event succeeded at 17:14:05 — router replicas=12

maria (oncall-sre): p99 now ~600ms for /v1/generate, streaming p99 ~1.1s still. we need to reduce tail latency on streaming — probable backlog/slow read on workers.

raj (eng-runtime): two candidate mitigations: 1) enable request-drop-policy for overloaded workers (reject new sessions to avoid head-of-line blocking), 2) swap model variant to quantized smaller model for streaming route as graceful degradation. both require brief config toggle. which first?

maria (oncall-sre): do 1) first — keep sessions alive for existing but stop accepting new until warmed. jim please flip drop policy.

jim (eng-platform): `routingctl set-policy --route /v1/stream --policy reject-new-if-inflight>200` -> applied at 17:15:12

ops-bot: policy applied. metric: new session rate dropped 85% within 30s.

lucy (customer-support): paste to customers: "We're routing new requests to alternative nodes and working to restore normal response times. Existing sessions should continue, but new sessions might see retries. We'll update in 10 minutes."

dan (product): prepare post-incident notes for SLA review: need timeline, root cause (cache thrash + node restarts + provider limit), and recommended fixes (pre-warming, quota work, retry/backpressure improvements).

maria (oncall-sre): live checklist: 
- [x] route fallback applied
- [x] router scaled
- [x] reject-new policy applied
- [ ] investigate root cause of pod OOMs (memory leak? model mem spike)
- [ ] follow-up: scheduling/quotas

raj (eng-runtime): quick memory profile from crashed worker: `heap: 7.2GB -> 11.4GB` during large-batch decode. config shows `max_batch_tokens=4096` — we temporarily lower to 2048 for streaming pool.

jim (eng-platform): applied config change to pool-us-east-2: `max_batch_tokens=2048` at 17:16:40. rolling restart scheduled with 30s stagger.

maria (oncall-sre): rolling restart in progress. watching for OOMs to stop.

ops-bot: worker restarts stabilized at 17:17:50, no new OOMs in last 6 mins.

maria (oncall-sre): p99 streaming now down to ~450ms, p95 ~120ms. customer reports of stalls reduced. recommending we keep reject-new policy for 15 more minutes and then ramp traffic back gradually.

lucy (customer-support): sending update to impacted customers: mitigation applied, performance improving, we will follow up with root cause and timeline.

dan (product): good. can someone add a quick notes thread for postmortem? include suggested action items: pre-warm caches on autoscaler events, set provider quota alerts, lower default batch_tokens for streaming pools, and improve graceful fallback to quantized models.

raj (eng-runtime): adding to backlog: implement local warm-up on scale and more conservative batch sizing policy per pool.

maria (oncall-sre): final steps for now: leave reject-new policy in place until 17:33, then incrementally shift 20%/30%/50%/100 back to pool-us-east-2 if metrics hold. monitoring manual for next 30m. handing back to oncall rotation.

maria (oncall-sre): paging clear? I'm leaving channel but will follow up on postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) at 17:18:30 — p99 restored below alert threshold. Please file postmortem if >30m customer impact.

lucy (customer-support): ticket notes updated and handoff to account reps done for enterprise-acme.

dan (product): thanks team — please capture timeline and decisions. I'll coordinate SLA messaging with legal for any billing adjustments. :thumbsup:

maria (oncall-sre): handing to next oncall (raj) with summary: root cause: worker OOMs triggered cache thrash -> queueing -> p99 spike. mitigations: route fallback, router scale, reject-new policy, lower batch_tokens, cache warm-up. follow-ups assigned to eng-runtime + eng-platform.

raj (eng-runtime): ack, will own runtime follow-ups. setting a recurring job to run cache-warm after scale events.

ops-bot: Handoff recorded. next-oncall: raj (eng-runtime).

maria (oncall-sre): thanks everyone — closing thread.
